name.value: Baseline group differences in cortical thickness

definition.value: Group differences in cortical thickness at baseline, with thinner cortices in cocaine users compared to controls.

spans.text: At baseline, significant group effects were found for CT in the SFG, and IFG as well as in the lateral OFC (F  = 5.59–6.83, P = .021–0.11;  Fig. 1 A and  Suppl. Table 1 ). In all of the analyzed ROI, thinner cortices were found in CU compared to controls.
We hypothesized CT/CSA in the six frontal regions of interest and cognitive performance to be lower in CU than in controls at baseline.
To extract CT and CSA for several regions of interests (ROI), the cortex was parcellated by the use of the Desikan-Killiany Atlas ( Desikan et al., 2006 ).
A total of 38 healthy controls and 29 CU were included in this study

value: At baseline, cocaine users displayed thinner cortices than controls in the superior frontal gyrus, inferior frontal gyrus, and lateral orbitofrontal cortex.
The larger the amount of cocaine used and the longer cocaine had been used, the thinner the lateral frontal regions were.

value: Decreasers significantly increased their cortical thickness within the superior, middle, and inferior frontal gyri, whereas cortical thickness in Sustained Users seemed to further decrease over time without reaching significance.

Decreased or ceased cocaine intake led to significant thickening of the lateral frontal cortex, whereas sustained use was associated, albeit not significantly, with further thinning within the same region.
